title: Codemagic Patch daily usage report (v1)
description: Wire contract for the usage report a Codemagic Patch server POSTs once per UTC day to the public collector (https://telemetry.codemagicpatch.dev/v1/report) when the usage report is enabled. The body is plain JSON, well under 8 KiB, and carries only per-day aggregate counts read from the server's own daily aggregate tables: never device, app, team, or deployment identifiers or names, URLs, emails, bundle hashes, or failure reasons. The root schema is the lenient envelope the collector enforces at runtime; `strictReport` is the exact shape current senders produce and is what the server's and the collector's contract tests validate fixtures against.
$comment: Evolution rules: additive-only within v1. The collector ignores unknown fields at every level and accepts any string in `instance.mode`, `instance.storage_adapter`, and `instance.delivery_adapter`, so a newer server never gets a 400 for a value this file does not list yet. `instance.hosting` stays an enum because it selects the collector's authentication. `schema_version` is bumped only for breaking changes.

schema_version.description: Wire-format major version. Always 1 for this schema.

instance_id.description: Random UUID minted once per installation, on the first report. The only identity in the report; it says nothing about the operator.

sent_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the sender built the report.

days.description: One row per UTC day, ascending. Servers transmit the previous UTC day, counted from the raw events that had arrived by the time of sending, and never re-send one; the collector accepts up to 31 rows for forward compatibility, replaces each (instance, day) pair it already holds, and ignores days outside its acceptance window one by one. A day a sender could not deliver stays missing for that instance.

instance.description: Coarse, non-identifying properties of the installation.

hosting.description: `self-hosted` is an operator-run install; `managed` is Codemagic's own multi-team service and must carry a bearer token the collector knows.

mode.description: `MODE` the process runs in. Current senders send `all` or `api`; a `worker` process never reports.

database.description: Whether the database is the bundled Compose Postgres or an operator-managed one, as the dashboard Status page derives it.

storage.description: Whether object storage is the bundled Compose MinIO, an external bucket, or `none` (the in-process memory adapter).

snapshot.description: Point-in-time totals at send time. The collector keeps only the latest snapshot per instance and never adds snapshots across days.

active_devices.description: Devices that sent `Active` that day: the sum of per-deployment distinct counts.

applied.description: `Applied` events with a target package hash, the success-rate numerator.

failed.description: `Failed` events with a target package hash, the other half of the success-rate denominator.

failed_unattributed.description: `Failed` events without a target package hash. Excluded from the success rate, kept so nothing is silently dropped.

releases.description: Releases created that day (published or disabled), excluding rollbacks.

rollbacks.description: Operator release rollbacks created that day (`rollback_of` set). Not SDK crash rollbacks.

active_teams.description: Teams with at least one metric event that day.

active_apps.description: Apps with at least one metric event that day.

strictReport.title: Daily usage report, exact shape of current senders
strictReport.description: What `buildTelemetryReport` in the server produces today: every field present, no extras, one day row, the previous UTC day (the deploy smoke sends none). Contract tests validate fixtures against this; the collector enforces only `report`.
